newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgeon says no surprises during Yeltsin operation.
newsitem.headline: Surgeon says no surprises during Yeltsin operation.

text.p: There were no surprises during Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation and all the signs indicate that his heart is now getting enough blood, surgeon Renat Akchurin told a news conference.

"Nothing extraordinary has emerged. All indications are that the heart muscle is getting enough blood to function normally," said Akchurin, who looked exhausted after seven hours of surgery. "Now the very important stage of post-operative treatment is starting."

Akchurin, speaking at the Cardiology Research Centre where surgery took place, had led Yeltsin's heart operation, which aimed to bypass clogged cardiac arteries and allow the Russian president, 65, to lead a normal life.

Doctors have said the post-operative stage is the one of most crucial parts of Yeltsin's treatment and specialists advising the Russian doctors on the operation include two German surgeons who have done a lot of work in this sphere.
Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told the news conference that the operation had ended successfully at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT). It started at 7 a.m. (0400 GMT).
